claim.pdf_says: '14.9.48.4   General rules' is printed in the four-level sub-subsection style, one level below '14.9.48 UNSTRING statement'.
claim.why_it_matters: Emitted at h2, level-equal with '## 14.9.48 UNSTRING statement' (line 32362), while its siblings 14.9.48.1 / .2 / .3 are correctly at h3 (lines 32365, 32370, 32395). The UNSTRING general rules therefore detach from the UNSTRING statement in the document outline.

verdict.reasoning: REFUTED on four independent grounds. (1) NOTHING IS MISSING. The claim is filed as kind=missing-heading, but the heading is present, complete, and verbatim correct. Rendered page 800 (E:/Temp/specrecon/v800/spec_p800.png, 300dpi) prints '14.9.48.4 General rules' immediately after Syntax rule 10 ('...shall not reference a variable-length group.'). specs/ISO_COBOL.md carries exactly that text at line 32432, preceded by a correct anchor '' at 32431. Title, number, ordinal position, and anchor all match the PDF. The sole difference is the markdown heading-depth token: '##' rather than '###'. (2) THE PDF DRAWS NO LEVEL DISTINCTION TO LOSE. I rendered the facing page 799 to compare the sibling headings directly. On page 799 ISO prints '14.9.48 UNSTRING statement', '14.9.48.1 General', '14.9.48.2 General format', and '14.9.48.3 Syntax rules' in one and the same style -- same bold serif face, same point size, same left margin, same trailing gap before the title. Page 800's '14.9.48.4 General rules' is that identical style. ISO's typography carries no depth signal here whatsoever; the hierarchy is conveyed entirely by the dotted section number, and the markdown reproduces that number exactly. The claim's premise that the PDF prints .4 'in the four-level sub-subsection style, one level below 14.9.48' asserts a typographic contrast that the printed glyphs do not contain -- 14.9.48 and 14.9.48.4 are set identically on the page. (3) IT IS A DOC-WIDE RENDERING ARTIFACT, NOT A PAGE-800 CONTENT DEFECT. Heading depth is assigned pseudo-randomly throughout the transcription. Within section 14.9 alone, 40 four-level headings are emitted at h2 and 162 at h3. The neighbours make this obvious: 14.9.47.1/.2/.3/.4 are all h3, 14.9.48.1/.2/.3 are h3 but .4 is h2, and 14.9.49.1/.2 are h3 while .3 and .4 are h2. Even the three-level statement headings vary -- '### 14.9.1 ACCEPT statement' versus '## 14.9.2 ADD statement'. Flagging this one instance as a page-800 discrepancy mistakes a global transcription-formatting characteristic for a localized loss of spec content. (4) THE CLAIM MISQUOTES ITS OWN EVIDENCE. Every line number cited is wrong by three. '## 14.9.48.4 General rules' is at line 32432, not 32429 (32429 is Syntax rule 10, body text). '## 14.9.48 UNSTRING statement' is at 32365, not 32362 (32362 is the running head '# ISO/IEC 1989:2023 (E)'). The siblings are at 32368 / 32373 / 32398, not 32365 / 32370 / 32395 -- the first of those cited lines is the UNSTRING statement heading itself. No normative text, no rule number, no rule wording, and no section identifier differs between the PDF and the markdown on page 800. Nothing a compiler-conformance reader would derive from 14.9.48.4 is altered or unreachable: the section is titled, numbered, anchored, and its ten general rules follow in order. This is markdown formatting, not spec content.
